TH Khan, with Md Rezaul Islam, Advocates-----For Petitioners.
Mrinal Kanti Biswas with Ambia Bulbul Reza, Advocates-----For the Opposite Party No. 1.
parties:
Khorshed  Ali and another ----- Petitioners
Vs
Syeda Sharfunnessa and another ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Syed AB Mahmudul Huq J : This rule was issued on 29-7-2007, by this Court on an application filed under section 439 of the CrPC by Md Khorshed Ali and another as petitioners, calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 18-7-2007, passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court Dhaka, allowing the Metro Criminal Revision No. 155 of 6, setting aside and reversing the order of discharge, dated 15-12-2005 passed by learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, arising out of Petition Case (CR) No. 1091 of 4, under sections 406/467/447/506 of the Penal Code should not be set aside. 

 2. The Opposite party No.1, of the revisional application, as a complainant filed the CR Case No. 1091 of 4 in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dhaka, for trial of the accused petitioners on the allegations inter alia that, the petitioner and her sister were owners of four annas share in their private properties, which were managed by the accused No.1, as a Mutawalli of the Khan Shaheb Haji Emdad Ali Waqf Estate, and the accused persons were utilizing the entire income without paying their share. All the sharers of the said property applied to the Administrator of Waqf, for an order, directing the accused persons to partition the entire property, and hand over the possession of their private property. In spite of the order of the Administrator of the Waqf, they were not doing so, and were not paying their shares of the income. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate by the order dated 12-5-2004, sent the same to the Officer-in-charge, Lalbagh Thana, directing him to conduct preliminary investigation and to start case under relevant sections of the Penal Code. After conducting proper investigation the report dated 16-9-04 was sent to the CMM by the Officer-in-Charge Lalbagh Thana, with a finding that over the same issue Civil Suit, being No. 38 of 2004, was pending and the parties were directed to take redress in the Civil Court. After getting the said report the CMM filed the case by the order dated 21-4-04. The complainant took up a Naraji Petition on 12-2-05, after about five months, against the filing of the complaint, and the Court by its order dated 19-2-05, sent the case record for judicial inquiry. The learned Magistrate after holding inquiry sent the case record to the CMM for proceeding with the case by the order dated 12-5-05, and the trial of the case proceeded. The accused petitioners entered appearance in the case and they filed an application for discharging them from the case. The accused were discharged from the case under section 241A of the CrPC, by the order dated 15-12-05. Thereafter, the Complaint moved a revisional application before the Sessions Judge below. The learned Addl. Sessions judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, after hearing the revisional application was pleased to allow the application. Against that order the petitioners obtained this Rule. 

 3. Mr TH Khan, the learned Senior Advocate, appearing for the petitioners in support of the rule submits that, the petition of complaint will show that the dispute is relating to an undivided, un-partitioned ejmali property, which is being managed by the Mutawalli, as Waqf Estate, and the dispute as has been raised, will show that, it is a civil dispute, which requires partition of the shares of the complaint, for which no criminal liability arises against the accused petitioners. The petitioner No. 1, is admittedly a Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate, while, the petitioner No. 2 is the manager of the same Waqf Estate, and they are acting as Mutawalli and manager of the Estate respectively. He submits, referring to a judgment passed by a Division Bench of this Court, where an FIR lodged by Alhaj Syeda Fa tema Faizunessa with the Lalbagh PS alleging that they are owners of the major shares of 7 and a half bighas of land, described in the FIR while the remaining other share is Waqf property. The petitioner is the Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate, who, by printing receipts of rent realized rents from the monthly tenants of the houses standing on the land, and have misappropriated Taka sixteen cores, collected as monthly rents from the tenants. On the basis of the said FIR, Lalbagh PS case No. 8, dated 3-7-8, under sections 420/447/467/468/471/506 of the Penal Code was started against the accused petitioners. The Mutawalli and another accused, preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.15319 of 2008 for quashing of the said Lalbagh Police Station Case No. 8 dated 3-7-2008, which was pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. The High Court Division after hearing the said rule was pleased to quash the proceeding by the judgment dated 13-1-2011, in Crl. Misc. Case No.15319 of 2008. 

 5. We have gone through the petition of complaint which has been annexed as Annexure-D, with the Supplementary Affidavit. In the petition of complaint in paragraph 2, the same assertion, as has been made in the FIR of the Lalbagh PS Case No.8, dated 3-7-2008, has been reiterated, claiming 7 and a half bighas of land. It has been admitted in the petition of complaint that 12 annas share of the property, is Waqf property, and the 4 annas share of the property is a secular property belonging to other sharers. It has been further stated that the Waqf Administrator made an order for partition of the property of the other sharers, and for giving them the shares, and there has been an order to give possession to them by the DC. The petition of complaint mentioned that in spite of the order of the Deputy Commissioner and the Waqf Administrator, the share of the other sharers was not paid by the accused. It has been further contended in the petition of complaint that the sharers were not given their shares. 

 7. As we have found from the judgment passed in Criminal Misc. Case No.15319 of 8, that on the same type of allegations, the FIR lodged by one of the co-sharer, Syeda Fatema Faizunnessa, daughter of Mir Md Khijir Ali, admittedly a co-sharer of the property had raised claim and made allegations against these petitioners of realization of the rents and misappropriation of the same rents. The proceedings of the said case was quashed under section 561A of CrPC with the findings that the Waqf Estate had share in the case property and that the petitioner No.1, the Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate had collected rents from the tenants of the house standing on the land. The alleged act, even if, is taken as true, does not constitutes any offence 

 8. We have gone through the order dated 15-12-05 passed by the Metropolitan Magistrate after hearing of the application filed under section 241A of CrPC. The learned Magistrate perused the record and submissions of the parties and found that there was a civil suit pending in the Court, and the proceeding of Criminal Case cannot proceed against the accused and he discharged the accused of the charges under sections 420/467/506 of the Penal Code. 

 "241A. When accused shall be discharged:—When the accused appears or is brought before the Magistrate, and if the Magistrate, upon consideration of record of the case and the documents submitted therewith and making such examination, if any, of the accused as the Magistrate thinks necessary and after giving the prosecution and the accused an opportunity of being heard, considers the charge to be groundless, he shall discharge the accused and record his reasons for so doing" 

 10. Considering the facts, as revealed in the petition of complainant and the findings of the High Court Division in Criminal Misc. case No. 15319/2008, we are of the view that it is a dispute relating a property belonging a part of it to the Waqf Estate, and a part of it is claimed, as private property, by co-sharers. There has been no partition thereof, by Mets and bounds, and the property is being managed as a Waqf property. And that the dispute is a civil dispute amongst the co-Sharers, and the Waqf Authority, and the same dispute is of a civil nature. 

 12. In the result, the rule is made absolute. The judgment passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, allowing the Metro Criminal Revision No 155 of 2006, reversing the order of discharge dated 15-12-05, by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, arising out of petition case No. 1091 of 04, is hereby set aside and the order of discharge dated 15-12-05, passed in the petition case is upheld.
